[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The runner Auto Scaling group can launch instances before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token exists, even though the source notes that the instance user-data manages this parameter's value. Ensure the parameter is created before the group starts its runner instance.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Auto Scaling group launches the runner instance, whose user-data script relies on the SSM parameter managed by this resource (the source comment says the parameter value is managed by user data). The group can launch the instance before the parameter exists; make the group wait for the parameter to be created.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The runner's user-data flow manages the registration token in this SSM parameter, but the Auto Scaling group does not wait for the parameter to exist before launching the instance. Initialization can attempt to write the token before the parameter is created.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The `aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token` is created by Terraform with value "null" and `ignore_changes` on `value`; the runner instance's user-data script is responsible for writing the actual registration token into it (per the source comment "Parameter value is managed by the user-data script"). The user-data script overwrites an existing parameter (`aws ssm put-parameter ... --overwrite`), which fails if the parameter does not yet exist. Since the autoscaling group boots the instance as soon as it is created and neither an attribute reference nor a depends_on ties it to the SSM parameter, the instance can start and fail its user-data registration before the parameter is created.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The runner agent instances boot from user data that registers the runner with GitLab and writes the resulting token into the SSM parameter `aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token` (the code comment states "Parameter value is managed by the user-data script of the gitlab runner instance"). The autoscaling group has no dependency on the SSM parameter, so instances can boot before Terraform creates the parameter. The user-data script (`put-parameter`) would then create the parameter itself, and Terraform's subsequent create of `aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token` would fail with a ParameterAlreadyExists error (the resource's `overwrite` defaults to false on create, per provider docs). The ASG should be ordered after the SSM parameter.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Auto Scaling group can launch the runner before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm attaches the token-management permissions to the instance role. Order runner startup after this attachment so user-data/token operations have the required permissions.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
When managed GitLab token storage is enabled, the runner user data needs the SSM permissions granted by this attachment. The Auto Scaling group can launch the runner before those permissions are attached; make it wait for the attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Auto Scaling group may launch the runner before this SSM policy attachment is ready, while the bootstrap flow is configured to manage the runner token in SSM. That can cause token management during initialization to fail.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Auto Scaling group can launch the runner before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy grants its instance role the policy needed to manage Docker Machine instances. Ensure the policy attachment is in place before runner instances start.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Auto Scaling group can launch the runner before the instance role receives the managed policy that permits the runner agent to create docker-machine instances. Make the group wait for this policy attachment before launching instances.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Auto Scaling group launches instances using the instance role, but does not wait for this role policy attachment to complete. A newly launched runner may begin operating before it has the permissions needed to manage Docker Machine instances.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The runner Auto Scaling group may launch instances before the inline CloudWatch logging policy is attached to their instance role. When logging is enabled, ensure this policy is in place before instances boot and initialize logging.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Auto Scaling group can launch the runner before its instance role has the CloudWatch logging inline policy. Since the instance user data configures logging, make group creation wait for this policy so startup does not race the policy creation.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Auto Scaling group may launch the runner before its inline CloudWatch logging policy is attached, so logging setup or log delivery during initialization can fail.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The runner Auto Scaling group may launch instances before the cache policy is attached to their instance role. A runner could begin work before it has the permissions needed to use the configured shared cache; order instance startup after this attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Auto Scaling group can launch the runner before its instance role receives the cache policy attachment, allowing the runner to become active before it has the configured cache access. Make group creation wait for the attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Auto Scaling group launches instances using the instance role, but does not wait for this cache policy attachment to complete. Runner jobs may start before the role has the cache permissions it needs.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
When service-linked-role creation is enabled, runner instances may start before the corresponding policy is attached to their role. Order the Auto Scaling group after this attachment so Docker Machine operations have the intended permissions.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
When service-linked-role creation is enabled, the runner instance needs this role-policy attachment to create service-linked roles. The Auto Scaling group can launch it before the permission is attached, so make group creation wait for the attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Auto Scaling group launches instances using the instance role, but does not wait for this optional service-linked-role policy attachment to complete. If enabled, runner activity requiring that permission can start before it is available.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_launch_configuration.gitlab_runner_instance carries the runner's user_data, which registers the runner and then stores the token into the SSM SecureString parameter named by local.secure_parameter_store_runner_token_key. The SSM parameter (aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token) is only referenced by name string, so nothing guarantees it exists before the instance boots. If the instance's user-data writes the token first and the Terraform-managed parameter (value = "null") is created afterward, it overwrites the token and breaks the runner. The launch configuration should depend on the SSM parameter.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token is created with value="null" and its real value is written by the runner instance's user-data script. If the parameter does not exist yet when Terraform later applies it, it can clobber the token written during registration. The launch configuration (which defines the instance's user-data) is not ordered after aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token. Add depends_on so the parameter exists before the runner instance is created.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
The runner's user_data accesses SSM (get/put the runner token) when enable_manage_gitlab_token is true, which requires the SSM access policy to be attached to the instance role. aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm attaches to aws_iam_role.instance in parallel with the instance profile, and the launch configuration waits only on the profile, so an instance can boot before the SSM policy is attached. The launch configuration should depend on the ssm policy attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The runner agent reads/writes the GitLab registration token in SSM, requiring the permissions from aws_iam_policy.ssm. The attachment is not ordered before the instance, so registration can fail if the policy is not yet attached. Order the launch configuration after aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm.

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
The runner's user_data includes the CloudWatch logging config (data.template_file.logging) that targets the log group named var.environment, which is created by aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment. That resource is referenced only by the environment name string, so nothing orders the launch configuration (and thus the instance launch) after the log group. The launch configuration should depend on the CloudWatch log group so it exists before the instance begins writing logs.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The runner instance configures Docker/CloudWatch logging to the log group aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment (name = var.environment), but the launch configuration does not wait for that log group to exist. If the group is absent when the agent starts logging, the awslogs driver fails. Add depends_on so the log group is created first.
